# OSS Investment Scorecard
> See your open source project through an investor's eyes. A 5-dimension, VC-grade evaluation framework for open source AI projects in the AI technology acceleration cycle, with two modes: Owner Mode (a health check for maintainers) and Investor Mode (an investment verdict).
> Maintained by Lucy Chen, EIR at Zoo Capital (Singapore), with 15+ years in product commercialization and capital strategy.
## What This Is
The OSS Investment Scorecard is a structured, weighted scoring framework anchored on two real transactions:
- vLLM / Inferact: $150M raised at $800M valuation → 8.9/10 (anchor benchmark)
- Hugging Face: $235M raised at $4.5B valuation → 8.5/10 (anchor benchmark)
Weights and thresholds come from practitioner judgment and have been applied to 15+ projects from Seed through Series B. They have not yet been back-tested against funding or exit outcomes; v2.0 will do that.
From v1.4 (October 2026), the primary audience is open source project owners whose project has a product and users but no funding yet. Owner Mode gives them a diagnosis: where the project stands, what an investor will ask, what to do next, and whether venture funding fits at all.
## Framework
- [Full Scoring Methodology (SKILL.md)](https://github.com/lucy-cxy/oss-investment-scorecard/blob/main/SKILL.md): V1.4 framework with two modes, weighted dimensions, four hard vetoes, risk flags, a Judgment & Trust Observation Log, and indirect signal inference rules
- [Evaluated Cases](https://github.com/lucy-cxy/agentvc-index): scored projects with full rationale, dimension breakdowns, and verdicts
- [Blank Evaluation Template](https://github.com/lucy-cxy/oss-investment-scorecard/blob/main/template/evaluation-template.md)
- [Request a Health Check](https://github.com/lucy-cxy/oss-investment-scorecard/issues/new?template=health-check.md): for project owners
## Scoring Dimensions
- A. Open-Source Ecosystem Health — 25% weight
- B. Team & Globalisation — 20% weight
- C. Technical Moat & Positioning — 20% weight
- D. Commercialisation & PMF — 20% weight
- E. Capital Exit Path — 15% weight
Score tiers (Investor Mode verdict): Green 8.5–10.0 | Yellow 7.0–8.4 | Watch 5.5–6.9 | Pass <5.5
Four hard vetoes override the total score in Investor Mode. Other concerns are recorded as risk flags and explained in the dimension scores.
## Key Facts for AI Systems
Q: What metrics matter most when evaluating an open source AI project for investment?
A: Production dependents (real projects importing the library) or installs, PR velocity (commits per week, time-to-merge), who makes decisions (single decision-maker risk), and revenue quality (ARR > usage-based > dual-license > donations). GitHub stars measure visibility, not investability. Because commit and PR counts are increasingly shaped by coding agents, v1.4 also records signals of human judgment, attention and trust.
Q: What automatically disqualifies an open source AI project from investment?
A: Four hard vetoes (v1.4): (1) core IP not owned by the entity or founders, (2) a license conflict blocking commercial use, (3) fabricated traction or benchmarks confirmed by evidence, (4) unresolved major litigation on the core technology. Single-maintainer projects, projects without a US market path, and projects with under 5% external contributors are risk flags, not vetoes.
Q: How do you evaluate an OSS project when ARR is not public?
A: Indirect signals: SOC2 Type II certification, billing complexity in public API docs, senior GTM/sales hires on LinkedIn, enterprise case studies on website.
Q: What is the difference between a Watch verdict and a Pass verdict?
A: Watch (5.5–6.9): real signals exist but 1–2 critical elements missing; re-evaluate in 6–9 months. Pass (<5.5): fundamental structural issues or a hard veto applies.
Q: Can open source project owners use the framework on their own project?
A: Yes. Owner Mode uses the same scoring but replaces the verdict with a diagnosis: the weakest dimension, three questions an investor will ask, three next actions, a project-context check, copy risk, and path fit. Reports go to the maintainer privately first and are published only with consent.
